string.text: SKS

A semi-automatic carbine designed by Soviet designer Simonov for mass-produced infantry units of the Red Army and adopted for service in 1949. Despite its superior accuracy, it was subsequently supplanted by the Kalashnikov assault rifle, which boasted a significantly superior firepower. Nevertheless, a large number of already produced carbines remained in military warehouses, from where they gradually found their way into the Zone through various routes.
Polymer buffer
Addition of a polymer buffer to the return mechanism reduces felt recoil.
Trigger calibration
Individual adjustment and balancing of the standard parts of the trigger mechanism improve accuracy, while simultaneously lowering recoil.
Faster twist rate
Increases muzzle velocity, thus improving the flatness of the trajectory. Useful for long range fire.
Barrel adjustment
Reduces bullet dispersion, which improves accuracy.
Bayonet

Equipping a weapon with a long bayonet allows you to expand the range of melee attacks and significantly increase the damage inflicted in them - especially if words like "humanity" and "mercy" towards your opponents don't mean much to you in practice.
Improved muzzle brake
Significantly reduces felt recoil and muzzle climb.
Improved gas block
The modification of the gas-operated mechanism increases the reliability of the automatic operation, reducing the number of misfires.
Tactical device
Insight AN/PEQ-16a tactical block combines the functions of a laser sight and a tactical flashlight. Particularly useful in night conditions.
Tritium sights
Tritium-illuminated sights increase speed and comfort of aiming in poorly-lit environments.
Dovetail rail
Equipping the weapon with a standard Soviet-type mount allows the installation of most optical sights adopted by Warsaw Pact countries.
Protective coating
Application of a protective coating to the internal parts significantly reduces wear.
Picatinny rail
Equipping the weapon with a standard Picatinny mount allows it to be fitted with most NATO optical sights.
Bolt adjustment
Exact fit of the bolt carrier group reduces play, which improves accuracy.
Balanced bolt
Balanced bolt carrier group reduces the muzzle climb, as well as reduces the probability of malfunctions.
Magazine feed system

Converting the standard cartridge feed mechanism to a magazine feed system allows for significantly faster reloads in combat, while a larger magazine, holding 20 rounds, reduces the number of such reloads.
Tactical set

Replacing standard wooden components with modern plastic ones reduces the weapon's weight and improves handling. Furthermore, the inclusion of Weaver mounts allows for the subsequent installation of additional tactical accessories and compatible sights.
Match trigger
Allows to significantly increase the practical rate of fire.
Lightweight parts
Reduces weight by replacing weapon parts with their light-alloy counterparts without any significant loss in other performance characteristics.
More durable parts
Parts have increased wear-resistance, which makes the gun more durable.
